question.title: Identify Consecutive Sequences
question.desc: Given a table of student IDs and their respective scores, identify the student IDs that have consecutive scores in ascending order. The sequence must be at least 3 scores long.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS student_scores; CREATE TABLE student_scores (student_id INTEGER, score INTEGER); INSERT INTO student_scores (student_id, score) VALUES (1, 10), (1, 20), (1, 30), (2, 5), (2, 10), (2, 15), (3, 20), (3, 25), (3, 30);
question.solution: WITH ranked_scores AS ( SELECT student_id, score, LAG(score) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY score) AS prev_score, LEAD(score) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY score) AS next_score FROM student_scores ) SELECT DISTINCT student_id FROM ranked_scores WHERE score - prev_score = 10 AND next_score - score = 10;
question.tips: Consider using window functions to compare adjacent scores.
hints: You will need to use window functions to compare scores.
Use LAG and LEAD functions to compare the current score with the previous and next scores.
Filter the results to include only student IDs where the difference between consecutive scores is 10.
